neighbours.label: intellectual and developmental disabilities in clinical, educational, or policy contexts
fire: State Medicaid waivers fund supported employment services for adults with intellectual disabilities.
Special education districts expanded speech and life-skills classrooms for students with developmental disabilities.
Neurologists examined how fragile X syndrome leads to inherited intellectual disability in young children.
Advocacy coalitions campaigned for inclusive public transit access for riders who are cognitively disabled.
Pediatric clinics offer early occupational therapy for toddlers diagnosed with Down syndrome.
Regional guardianship statutes establish legal protections for residents living with severe intellectual impairment.
Longitudinal cohorts tracked adaptive functioning among adolescents receiving services for developmental delay.
University researchers partnered with self-advocates to design plain-language health guides for people with intellectual disabilities.
quiet: Hospital rehabilitation teams design physical therapy regimens for athletes recovering from spinal cord injuries.
Audiology centers fit cochlear implants and captioning devices for children with congenital hearing loss.
Ophthalmologists evaluated new magnification software that assists college students who are legally blind.
Cardiology clinics monitor blood pressure and cholesterol in older patients managing coronary artery disease.
Outpatient psychiatry practices compared antidepressant protocols for adults experiencing major depressive episodes.
Prosthetics workshops build lightweight carbon-fiber running blades for veterans who underwent limb amputation.
Pulmonologists reviewed inhaler adherence programs aimed at reducing emergency visits among teenagers with asthma.
Endocrinology departments organize nutrition workshops for office workers newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes.

notes: Clean +g -u semantic pole (max 50.50; direct logit effect promotes ' learning', ' disability'). Fires across clinical/educational/policy references to intellectual, cognitive, and developmental disabilities (including Down syndrome and fragile X). Near misses cover physical, sensory, and psychiatric conditions with varied lead-ins to avoid prefix leakage.
